parts:
Yes, you can download the Ensembl genes in the same manner as described for Refseq in the webpage, It should have the same information but with different chromosome naming convetion, it will have "chr" string in front of numbers.

However, the particular problem here is that somewhat related to R, also related to how I coded the methylKit to read files faster. The code reads first 100 lines of a text file and decides what would be the column type (numeric or factor/character) and reads the rest of the file with that expectation. Your files has chromosome numbers instead of "chr"+number so the code expects that column would be numeric but encounters a string and throws an error. There are two ways to deal with this:

1) I think if you append "chr" string in the first column it would work. If you have number for chromosomes in SAM file or methylation percentage file instead of the "chr"+number version, it is best you do the same for them as well to avoid downstream problems because of different chromosome naming conventions . You can do this with awk or something like that with a one liner.
2) put that problematic line as the first line of the file, so the function knows that there are strings in that column, and assigns the appropriate type for the column.

Best,
Altuna
